$comment: What each library mutation may ask of the filesystem authority on the 386-directory profile (project-library fast-path blueprint FW0; lowered by FW2, the discovery index, and FW3, targeted verification), held by discovery-budget.test.ts. A ceiling only goes down: a count above it fails, and a count below it fails until the ceiling is lowered to match. FW2 traded one row's scan for a verification (delete-copy's post-delete proof of the route's copy), so its `verifications` rose while its discovery reads fell from 1,550 to 4. FW3 replaces delete-copy's two verifications with two probes: the library's of the other copy before the journal, and the authority's under the same hold of the project's lock as the removal; with the target's own 5 checks, which the filesystem cost test holds and this file does not charge, a copy's delete was 9 discovery reads, and a sole copy's is those 5 and one identity sweep. The FW3 review (M1) lists a surviving copy's root so the copy counts only when that root names it exactly and it is not the target under another spelling, but only for a copy in the target's own root that a caller or the index nominated: this row's other copy is in another root, so it stays at 9. FW3 raises three rows on purpose, by the blueprint's budget table: use-this-folder binds a route only to a directory a probe reads holding the id (2 reads, where FW2's warm pass decided from the index, which may only nominate), and create and duplicate allocate their directory against one fresh listing of the root's child names (1 listing, where FW2 read the index's names). The unit rows (`scan`, a full read of every directory; `warmPass`; `directoryRead`, one directory a warm pass re-reads; `sweep`, one `verifyAbsent`; `verification`; `probe`, one known location read under its locks; `listing`, one fresh listing of a root's names) are measured by packages/filesystem/src/project-directories.discovery-cost.test.ts into packages/filesystem/src/testing/discovery-unit-cost.json, which discovery-budget.test.ts holds these rows to; a change there changes them here. A discovery read is a file read or listing made to learn what a project directory holds. A record read is one `tau.json` read through the record client, outside a pass, a sweep or a verification.
